LanguageData.RW_WorldShapeTip: Ring: a closed loop of land around a sun, seen from its centre. Planet: the vanilla globe.
LanguageData.RW_RingSizeTip: Tiles around the whole ring × tiles from one rim to the other. Hexes are vanilla-sized, so the ring's size sets how big it looks. Only the land coverage's share of it has tiles; that tile count is shown here, and more tiles are slower to generate and play.
LanguageData.RW_LandCoverageTip: How much of the ring's loop has tiles. Below 100%, all the land is on one stretch of the ring centred on 0°; the rest of the ring is still there but has no tiles. A big ring at low coverage looks huge for a playable tile count.
LanguageData.RW_ConfirmLargeRing: This ring has {0} tiles, more than {1} (about a vanilla planet at 100% coverage). Generating and playing it may be slow.\n\nGenerate it anyway?
LanguageData.RW_LastChoiceWorld_Ring: This world is a Ring ({0}, {1} coverage), the last choice on the Create World page.
LanguageData.RW_LastChoiceWorld_Planet: This world is a Planet, the last choice on the Create World page.
LanguageData.RW_RingSizeLargeWarning: Over {0} tiles (about a vanilla planet at 100% coverage): generation and play may be slow.
LanguageData.RW_SettingSpillMountainsTip: Place spill mountains along the wall foot of new ring worlds. Worlds already generated keep what they were made with.
LanguageData.RW_SettingGhostIconsTip: Show faint icons of the places on the ring below in the orbit view and the atmosphere zoom bands. Applies immediately in every save.
LanguageData.RW_SettingCloudDensityTip: How cloudy the ring looks from orbit, from 0% (no clouds) to 200%. Applies immediately in every save.
LanguageData.RW_LaoLayerTab_SurfaceDescription: The ring's inner surface: a vast band of rock, soil and sea laid over the engineered scrith floor of the ring, pressed down by its spin and held in by the towering rim walls on either side. Here oceans meet land and every biome lies spread along the loop, warmest along the midline and coldest against the rims, beneath a sun that never sets and is only hidden by the passing shadow squares.
LanguageData.RW_LaoLayerTab_WorldDescription: A distant, sparsely populated ringworld at the edge of known space, built by an ancient civilization. A band of scrith spinning around its sun, so vast that its far side hangs in the sky as an arch. Lacking a central government or interstellar law, its inhabitants, many of them survivors of crashed starships, scrape out a living in a lawless, untamed landscape among the relics of builders far more advanced than they will ever be.
